errors: The deduction 'a) and b) imply S'_K ∩ S(K) = S(K) ∩ L' needs one more fact: vertices of K are never critical points of odd order (or not in the removed set). Otherwise a) would remove some vertices of L from S'. This is presumably part of the definition of C_K (critical points lie in edge interiors) but is not stated on the page.
Condition c) is left incomplete. The sentence trails off after 'de cardinal égal : i(s)' with crossed-out continuations, so the relation between i(s) and ν(s) is not established here.

The order of the boundary polygon ('2α_x') and the midpoint condition are only partly legible. The precise rule for S'' is unclear and may be inconsistent with b) for faces whose boundary sides contain no point of L.

ideas.what: Marking a cell decomposition from a pseudoline arrangement with two point sets S', S''. S' cuts each face boundary into a 2α-gon, and S'' gives one 'midpoint' per side (a barycentric-type, antipodally symmetric marking).
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision / flag-type marking of an arrangement's cell complex (cf. barycentric subdivision, medial constructions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard combinatorial topology; unsure of a specific source

ideas.what: Combinatorial critical points on the 1-skeleton with weights and signs. Their index i(s) is defined as the number of marked points between the nearest L-points on either side.
ideas.modern_name: Discrete inflection points / combinatorial index of critical points (cf. discrete Morse-type indices; discrete Möbius and four-vertex theorems)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discrete Morse theory: Forman (1995). Discrete inflection/flattening theorems for polygons and pseudoline-type curves: Arnold, Tabachnikov, Ovsienko and others (1990s onward).

ideas.what: Global lower bounds and antipodal relations for critical points on each face boundary (previous/next pages), here given a precise marking set-up.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial analogue of Möbius' theorem (at least 3 inflections of a non-contractible curve in RP^2) / Sturm–Hurwitz type bounds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Möbius (1852); modern discrete versions Arnold, Tabachnikov (1990s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a discrete index theory for 'critical points' of curves relative to a pseudoline arrangement. This page fixes the marked sets S', S'' and an index i(s) defined by counting marked points between the nearest L-points. The intended theorems (lower bounds, sign/antipode relations, behaviour under the face involution σ_-) are only partially formulated on adjacent pages. The thread appears not to have been completed or published.
missed.quote: l'intersection [t',t''] ∩ S'_K est de cardinal égal : i(s)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial Möbius/inflection theorem for pseudolines and arrangements, with an index calculus, is in the spirit of later work on discrete inflections and the combinatorics of oriented matroids. Grothendieck's specific formalism (weighted critical points, antipodal signs, transfer across faces) is undocumented. Whether it yields anything beyond known results is unclear from this page alone.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a definitional set-up in a known (archival) but unpublished Grothendieck project on pseudoline systems. The discrete index and critical-point formalism is mildly interesting as a possible precursor of discrete inflection/Morse-type ideas. However, the page itself contains no completed result and much is illegible or crossed out.
transcription_corrections: 'ensemble des pts critiques de K puissance[?] d'ordre impair': likely 'pts critiques de K de poids (ν) impair' or 'pris d'ordre impair'. In any case it refers to the weight/order ν(s) from the previous page.
'polygone top. d'ordre 2α': the image shows a subscript, '2α_x' (or 2ν_x), not a plain 2α.
'qui est son milieu si α est contenu[?]': the condition is unclear, possibly 'si ... est contenu dans L'.
'Pour toute arête (cour.) α de K, on α∩S'_K ≠ ∅' should read 'on a α ∩ S'_K ≠ ∅ dans [le] cas ... des arêtes de K'.
The inserted line '{+les sommets rouges sont pts rouges+}' is doubtful. It likely says the marked vertices (drawn in red) belong to S'.
